'''Versé''', formerly known as '''Versaat''',<ref name="Queen's Shadow" /> was a [[human]]<ref name="Episode II" /> [[Gender|female]] who was the niece of [[Mariek Panaka]], a [[captain]] in the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces]] and the [[Marriage|wife]] of Captain [[Quarsh Panaka]]. Versé was recommended by Panaka to join [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]]'s new cohort of [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens|Handmaidens]]. She was a top-notch [[slicer]] and used her talents in Amidala's service in more ways than one.<ref name="Queen's Shadow" />

In [[22 BBY]],<ref name="Date" /> Versé and her fellow handmaiden [[Cordé]] were [[Death|killed]] when the [[Starship|ship]] they had traveled to the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] on was destroyed by the [[bounty hunter]] [[Zam Wesell]] in an [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala|attempt]] to kill Amidala and prevent her from voting against the [[Military Creation Act]].<ref name="Episode II" />

{{Char-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
Versé was portrayed by [[Avril Wynne]] in the [[2002]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], the second installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]].<ref name="Royal Handmaidens Guide">{{SW|url=news/a-guide-to-the-royal-handmaidens|text=A Guide to the Royal Handmaidens of Naboo}}</ref> As Wynne remained uncredited until [[2019]] and her face was mostly obscured throughout her sole scene in ''Attack of the Clones'', author [[E. K. Johnston]] opted to substitute a new person as inspiration for the character's physical appearance when writing ''[[Queen's Shadow]]''. Johnston sought to create a more racially diverse cast in ''Queen's Shadow'' than found in the films and based Versé's appearance on a tour guide she had at [[Wikipedia:Rotorua|Rotorua]], [[Wikipedia:New Zealand|New Zealand]]. Johnston envisioned the character as stockier in build than her fellow [[Naboo Royal Handmaidens]] and portrayed by an actress of [[Wikipedia:Māori people|Māori]] descent, much like Queen [[Apailana]]'s actress, [[Keisha Castle-Hughes]].<ref name="QSCRG">{{Tumblr|subdomain=ekjohnston|url=post/183407684587/the-queens-shadow-character-reference-guide|name=Words Words Words|text=The Queen's Shadow Character Reference Guide|quote=The only handmaiden I had a bit of wiggle room with was '''Versé'''. Her actress is uncredited and we only see her very briefly on the ramp before the explosion. Even the RHS struggled to get a good view of her face, and trust me when I tell you that they are ''very'' good at that sort of thing. For this reason, I decided to sub in a new person, and based her on the tour guide I had at Rotorua, NZ. Versé is stockier than the others (because she never has to double for Padmé), and she's not white. I hesitate to say she's Maori, because SPACE, but she'd definitely be played by a Maori actress if the book was made into a movie.|archivedate=20190314050044|archivefile=File:Verse_appearance.png}}</ref>

Johnston also toyed with the possibility of making Versé a [[Wikipedia:Transgender|transgender]] woman in ''Queen's Shadow'', but decided against including it openly in the novel because at the time of writing it she did not feel she could do it justice.<ref name="Versé transgender">
{{Twitter|ek_johnston|status/1213229468942102528|[[E. K. Johnston]]|quote=I'm going to be really honest with you: I chickened out of making Versé openly trans bc I wasn't good enough to do her justice. It means nothing, but I am a better writer now, and next time I'll suck less. But yeah, Padmé would be down.|archivedate=20200104191818}}</ref> The author later indicated that she personally viewed Versé as trans,<ref name="Tweet">{{Twitter|ek_johnston|status/1214353884795174912|[[E. K. Johnston]]|quote=Versé is trans (I cannot stress enough how little credit I deserve for that as it isn't actually "in canon"), and Tonra is bi/pan, same as Sabé.|date=2020-01-06|archivedate=20200112220721|nolive=1}}</ref> in her heart, but noted that aspect of her character never made it in the finished work.<ref name="Tweet2">{{Twitter|ek_johnston|status/1214351585070829568|[[E. K. Johnston]]|quote=Sabé, Yané, and Saché on the page, Versé and Tonra in my heart.|date=2020-01-06|archivedate=20200114174204|nolive=1}}</ref>

In an interview, Johnston stated that she explicitly chose to include a scene—ultimately a conversation between Amidala and [[Rush Clovis]]—due to ''Queen's Shadow'' not having any trans characters. She indicated that she had originally started working on Versé being trans in the novel, saying that since the actor playing the character in ''Attack of the Clones'' was not clearly visible, she had more room to work with while drafting a story. However, Johnston noted that she quickly realized she did not want to pursue the concept for two reasons, one being that she wanted the first time she wrote a trans character to mean something the first time she wrote one for ''Star Wars'', instead of it being a brief mention. Secondly, the author felt strongly that she could not make Versé trans because she [[canon]]ically dies, as it would be disappointing to readers if such a character was introduced and then swiftly killed off. Instead, Versé was given a backstory as a skilled slicer, though her origins still reflected a similar [[Wikipedia:Character arc|character arc]] to Nomi Marks from the [[Netflix]] series [[Wikipedia:Sense8|''Sense8'']], who is a transgender character.<ref name="RebelLegion Interview">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@RebelLegionOfficial|link=Rebel Legion|video=fqN5UDaVz3c|text=15 Johnston Interview Trim|date=2022-05-10|archivedate=20231219162733}}</ref>
